column1: # Notices written inside a linked crate's source files that the crate's own
# license files don't carry: code or text the crate took from elsewhere, under
# that notice's terms. Also notice files a crate ships under a name
# rust_crates.py doesn't take for a license file (aec3's PATENT, Google's
# WebRTC patent grant). rust_crates.py copies each block unchanged to
# <crate>-<version>/<file>.notice.txt and cites it in the crate's entry.
# Tab-separated: crate, version, file (relative to the crate's folder), lines
# (first-last, counted from 1), marker (text that must be inside those lines,
# so a different block is never copied), evidence.
# rust_crates.py also scans every linked crate's compiled source files for
# license grants whose conditions bind binary copies (SOURCE_GRANTS: MIT, ISC,
# BSD's binary-form clause, W3C). A grant the crate's license texts don't
# carry must be inside a block listed here, or the notices fail to build — so
# a crate update that adds one can't slip through. Rows name an exact version:
# after an update, check the new version's file and update the row.

column6: BSD-2-Clause-style notice for Dmitry Vyukov's intrusive MPSC queue, which the file is based on; the crate's license files are MIT and Apache-2.0
W3C Software and Document License and W3C short notice for the UI Events KeyboardEvent key and code values that the Key and KeyCode enums are derived from; tao's license files don't carry them

Google's WebRTC patent grant, which aec3 (a Rust port of WebRTC AEC3) ships in its own PATENT file beside its LICENSE; that file name is not one rust_crates.py picks up as a license file, so this row copies it out whole
